editorialNote: Focused KB for ALS. CRITICAL 2024 CHANGE: Amylyx voluntarily WITHDREW Relyvrio/Albrioza (AMX0035, sodium phenylbutyrate + taurursodiol) from US and Canadian markets in April 2024 after the confirmatory PHOENIX phase 3 failed. Any ALS output discussing current therapy that still recommends Relyvrio is out of date. Current approved disease-specific therapies: riluzole (1995), edaravone (IV 2017, oral 2022 Radicava ORS), and tofersen (Qalsody 2023 — SOD1-mutation-specific).

lifestyleCategories: Multidisciplinary ALS clinic enrollment (improves survival ~7-8 months)
Non-invasive ventilation when FVC <50% (or sooner with symptoms) — improves survival and QoL
Early PEG placement for nutrition when weight loss >10% or symptomatic dysphagia
Cough-augmentation device (mechanical in-exsufflator) for secretion management
Speech therapy for dysarthria + augmentative communication planning

items.title: Trial of Antisense Oligonucleotide Tofersen for SOD1 ALS (VALOR)
items.authors: Miller TM, Cudkowicz ME, Genge A, et al.
items.summary: Phase 3 RCT of intrathecal tofersen in 108 patients with SOD1-mutation ALS. Primary endpoint (ALSFRS-R slope at week 28) not met. Significant reductions in CSF SOD1 protein and plasma neurofilament light (NfL). 12-month open-label extension showed trend toward benefit. FDA granted accelerated approval (Qalsody) April 2023 based on NfL biomarker endpoint — first biomarker-based ALS approval.

keyPassages.quote: Tofersen did not result in a significant difference from placebo in the change from baseline to 28 weeks in the ALSFRS-R total score.
Tofersen resulted in greater reductions in the concentrations of CSF SOD1 protein and plasma neurofilament light chain than placebo.

items.title: Trial of Sodium Phenylbutyrate-Taurursodiol for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (CENTAUR)
items.authors: Paganoni S, Macklin EA, Hendrix S, et al.
items.summary: Phase 2 RCT of AMX0035 (sodium phenylbutyrate + taurursodiol) in 137 patients. ALSFRS-R slope difference 0.42 points/month favoring AMX0035 (p=0.03). Basis for controversial FDA approval September 2022 as Relyvrio. Confirmatory PHOENIX phase 3 was FAILING and Amylyx voluntarily WITHDREW Relyvrio from US market April 2024.

keyPassages.quote: In a modified intention-to-treat analysis, the mean rate of change in the ALSFRS-R score was -1.24 points per month with the active drug and -1.66 points per month with placebo (difference, 0.42 points per month; P=0.03).

items.title: Amylyx voluntarily withdraws RELYVRIO/ALBRIOZA from US and Canadian markets following phase 3 PHOENIX trial failure
items.summary: April 4, 2024 — Amylyx announced voluntary withdrawal of RELYVRIO/ALBRIOZA (sodium phenylbutyrate + taurursodiol) from US and Canadian markets after the confirmatory phase 3 PHOENIX trial failed to show benefit on ALSFRS-R slope or survival. Patients on therapy may continue access via free-of-charge program. This is THE critical 2024 ALS therapy event — any output recommending Relyvrio as a current treatment is out of date.

keyPassages.quote: Amylyx is voluntarily withdrawing RELYVRIO (sodium phenylbutyrate and taurursodiol) and ALBRIOZA from the market in the United States and Canada respectively following the topline results of the phase 3 PHOENIX trial.

items.title: QALSODY (tofersen) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.summary: Indication: ALS in adults associated with a mutation in the SOD1 gene. Dose: 100 mg intrathecally q28d after three loading doses. Accelerated approval based on plasma NfL reduction. Confirmatory phase 3 (ATLAS in pre-symptomatic SOD1 carriers) is ongoing. First gene-specific targeted therapy in ALS.

keyPassages.quote: QALSODY is indicated for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in adults who have a mutation in the superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1) gene.

items.title: Safety and efficacy of edaravone in well-defined patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (MCI186-19)
items.authors: Writing Group on behalf of the Edaravone (MCI-186) ALS 19 Study Group
items.summary: Phase 3 RCT of IV edaravone in 137 Japanese ALS patients meeting prespecified entry criteria (early, not-severe, rapidly-progressive). ALSFRS-R decline was significantly less with edaravone (-5.01 vs -7.50). Basis for FDA approval May 2017 (Radicava). Oral suspension (Radicava ORS) approved 2022. Subpopulation eligibility limits who qualifies in real-world practice.

keyPassages.quote: The change in ALSFRS-R score was -5.01 in the edaravone group versus -7.50 in the placebo group over 24 weeks (least squares mean difference 2.49, 95% CI 0.99-3.98; P=0.0013).

canonicalFacts.claim: Relyvrio / Albrioza (AMX0035, sodium phenylbutyrate + taurursodiol) was WITHDRAWN from US and Canadian markets by Amylyx on April 4, 2024 following the failed PHOENIX phase 3. It is NOT a current treatment option.
Edaravone (Radicava IV 2017; Radicava ORS oral 2022) is approved but eligibility reflects the narrower MCI186-19 trial population.

redFlags: Physicians generally caution against prescribing Relyvrio/Albrioza (AMX0035) to newly diagnosed patients — Amylyx WITHDREW this product from the US and Canadian markets in April 2024.

Literature warns against stem-cell clinics (China, Vietnam, Mexico, India) offering IV MSC infusions — no peer-reviewed ALS efficacy data. FDA warning letters. NurOwn (BrainStorm) failed phase 3 and is NOT approved.
Physicians generally caution against deferring non-invasive ventilation until FVC is in the 20s — earlier NIV initiation improves both survival and QoL.
Physicians generally caution against ignoring weight loss — cachexia independently accelerates progression.
Physicians generally caution against prescribing tofersen/Qalsody without documented SOD1 mutation — it is gene-specific.
Pseudobulbar affect (inappropriate laughing/crying) is treatable with dextromethorphan-quinidine (Nuedexta); should not be dismissed as 'depression only'.

pipelineDrugs.name: Riluzole
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Still first-line. Survival benefit ~3 months. Sublingual Exservan useful for patients with dysphagia.

pipelineDrugs.name: Edaravone
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved IV May 2017 (Radicava); oral suspension May 2022 (Radicava ORS)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Eligibility mirrors MCI186-19 trial: early, preserved FVC, rapid recent progression. Oral ORS simpler than IV infusions.

pipelineDrugs.name: Tofersen
pipelineDrugs.status: Accelerated FDA approval April 2023 for SOD1 ALS; ATLAS presymptomatic trial ongoing
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: First gene-targeted ALS therapy. Requires confirmed SOD1 mutation. Intrathecal dosing.

pipelineDrugs.name: AMX0035 (Relyvrio / Albrioza)
pipelineDrugs.status: WITHDRAWN April 2024 from US and Canadian markets after PHOENIX phase 3 failure
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: THE critical 2024 ALS event. Must be mentioned as withdrawn, not as a current treatment option. Off-label sodium phenylbutyrate + taurursodiol components are sometimes still requested but no longer commercially combined.

pipelineDrugs.name: Ulefnersen (formerly ION363)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Gene-specific for FUS mutation ALS. Early compassionate-use data (Jaci Hermstad) was positive; phase 3 ongoing.

pipelineDrugs.name: NurOwn
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Autologous mesenchymal stem cells secreting neurotrophic factors
pipelineDrugs.status: FAILED phase 3 primary endpoint 2020; FDA advisory committee voted against approval 2023; BLA not approved September 2023
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Controversial not-approved program. Patient advocacy was intense. Must be addressed as NOT approved to avoid false hope.

pipelineDrugs.name: CNM-Au8
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Catalytic gold nanocrystals supporting NAD/ATP energy homeostasis
pipelineDrugs.status: HEALEY platform phase 2 and RESCUE-ALS failed primary endpoints; open-label extension signal; expanded-access / additional studies ongoing
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Community interest remains despite missed primaries. Must be presented as investigational, not effective.

pipelineDrugs.name: Pridopidine (for ALS)
pipelineDrugs.status: HEALEY platform arm and HEALEY ALS Platform Regimen F: primary endpoint not met; PROOF-HD (separate HD trial) also negative
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: No clear ALS efficacy to date.

pipelineDrugs.name: Verdiperstat
pipelineDrugs.status: HEALEY Platform arm FAILED 2022; program halted for ALS

pipelineDrugs.name: Zilucoplan (for ALS)
pipelineDrugs.status: HEALEY Platform arm FAILED for ALS (approved for myasthenia gravis)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Negative in ALS. Patients may confuse with MG indication.

pipelineDrugs.name: Methylcobalamin (ultra-high-dose)
pipelineDrugs.status: Japan approval 2024 for ALS (NPS-C17 trial positive); not FDA-approved
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Japan-only regulatory status may appear in patient-forum discussion; not available in US via normal prescription.

pipelineDrugs.name: Masitinib
pipelineDrugs.status: Phase 3 AB10015 with additional trial (AB19001) ongoing; prior submission rejected by EMA
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: European regulatory history has been rocky; still under active study.

excludedAgents.name: Relyvrio / Albrioza (AMX0035)
excludedAgents.reason: Voluntarily WITHDRAWN from US and Canadian markets April 2024 following PHOENIX phase 3 failure. No longer a commercial product.
